_README: FROZEN HASH VECTORS - anti-drift guard for manifest-aware versioning.
Each entry is a representative `contract` input plus its `overall_hash` computed
ONCE by the current hashing pipeline (agentversion/hasher.py :: hash_manifest,
still equals these literals. Unlike the self-referential example-manifest test, these
literals do NOT flow through the current code, so a silent canonicalization or
IF THIS TEST FAILS: a change altered the hash output. That is a BREAKING change to
manifest identity (every previously-stored overall_hash would no longer reproduce). Do NOT just
regenerate these vectors to make the test green. Either revert the change, or, if the
algorithm change is deliberate, bump the hash/format version (identity.hash_algorithm,
currently 'jcs-sha256') and regenerate these vectors as part of that intentional
Regenerate (only when intentional): see the docstring in test_frozen_hash_vectors.py.

minimal_contract.description: Baseline: three plain surfaces, no quantization or stripping.

float_quantization.description: generation_config float quantization (temperature 0.71->0.7, top_p 0.92->0.90) is part of the hashed identity.

runtime_only_stripping.description: Runtime-only keys (max_retries/timeout/batch_size) are stripped before hashing, at both the surface and generation_config level.

skill_registry.description: The skill_registry surface participates in overall_hash (skills hashed as-is, no quantization).

unicode_and_key_order.description: JCS canonicalization: Unicode/UTF-8 string handling and alphabetical key sorting (keys are intentionally shuffled in the input).
